title: Commitment routing, invoice-exception flow, and automated allocation tagging
creator: Marina Ortega
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request bespoke commitment routing and invoice exceptions tied to marketplace credits and partner offsets. Current intake is ad hoc: finance manually approves exceptions, engineering builds point solutions, and the console lacks a predictable decision flow. This causes billing delays, mismatched chargeback tags, and manual reconciliation for marketplace offsets.

Goal: Define a deterministic intake and prioritization workflow for pricing and billing non-bug requests that: 1) classifies requests by revenue/risk impact, 2) standardizes an invoice-exception decision path, and 3) automates cost-allocation tagging for commitments and marketplace offsets so downstream finance and customer success can reconcile without engineering intervention.

Scope: This ticket covers the product playbook and routing rules (not the full engineering implementation). Deliverables: routing matrix, approval SLAs, console UI wireframes for an 'Invoice Exception' intake form, standardized tag mapping for automated allocation, and a runbook for finance/CS to execute exceptions. Engineering tickets for implementation will be created as follow-ups.

Out of scope: changes to core pricing model, changes to billing infrastructure, or on-prem billing integrations (these will be separate epics).
acceptance_criteria: A routing matrix that maps request types to decision paths (auto-approve, CS approval, finance approval, exec review) exists and is reviewed by Finance and Legal.

A draft intake form (console + email template) is available that captures required fields for an invoice exception (customer, commitment id, term, requested adjustment, marketplace offset reference, accounting tag, justification, supporting docs).
A mapping table for automated allocation tags (commitment -> product_tag -> GL code) is produced and validated with Finance; at least 90% of historical exceptions map cleanly using the table.
Runbook with SLAs: Triage within 24h, decision within 5 business days for low/medium impact, 48h for high impact, and stakeholder notification templates are defined.
Sign-off from Finance, Revenue Ops, Customer Success, and Legal on the final playbook document.
tasks: Interview finance (Ava Patel) and revenue ops (Diego Morales) to capture current exception handling and reconciliation pain points
Analyze last 12 months of billing exceptions and marketplace credits to classify frequency, cost, and tag mapping failure modes
Draft routing matrix and decision criteria (impact thresholds: revenue delta, legal risk, data residency)
Prototype intake form fields and sample UI copy; coordinate with Design for wireframes
Create tag mapping table and run a dry-run mapping against 6 months of historical exceptions
Publish playbook in Confluence and schedule review meeting with cross-functional stakeholders
Spin up follow-up ENG tickets for automation and console work (batch & realtime allocation tagging, intake form backend)
Prepare communication plan for customers and internal teams once playbook is live
stakeholders: Sofia Nguyen - Head of Customer Success

notes:
Trade-offs considered: 1) aggressive automation may mis-map unusual marketplace offsets — mitigation: conservative auto-approve thresholds and manual review queue for edge cases; 2) adding too many intake fields increases friction — mitigation: present smart defaults and allow CS to 'fast-track' known partners.

Next steps post-playbook: open ENG epic for console intake + backend mapping service, and pilot with two enterprise customers (one with marketplace partner credits) to validate mapping accuracy and SLA targets.
